proposed_changes.before: Council concern about the pace of data center development in the city, following the Google data center already under construction in southeast Fort Wayne
proposed_changes.after: The proposal’s recitals sought time to review data-center definitions, development standards and impacts on electrical capacity, water and wastewater systems, public infrastructure, land and community resources while the zoning code lacked comprehensive standards for large-scale data-center development.

proposed_changes.before: Would not affect the existing Google data center project under construction in southeast Fort Wayne
proposed_changes.after: The rejected proposal concerned final discretionary Common Council approvals for new hyperscale or large-scale data-center developments, aggregating related phases, expansions and facilities under common ownership/control, contiguous sites, shared infrastructure or the same planned development. facts.value: Fort Wayne City Council regular session, October 13, 2026, at 5:30 p.m., Room 35, Citizen Square.

facts.value: Rejected: the amended data center moratorium resolution failed 4–4.
facts.supporting_summary: The minutes explicitly mark the proposal failed; this is not an enacted 365-day pause.

facts.value: Ayes: Rohli Booker, Paul Ensley, Russ Jehl, Geoff Paddock. Nays: Martin Bender, Michelle Chambers, Nathan Hartman, Scott Myers. Absent: Thomas Freistroffer. Mayor signature: N/A.

facts.value: Regulations Committee; Rohli Booker was listed as committee chair and representative.
facts.supporting_summary: The entry identifies the committee and lists Booker in both roles.

facts.value: The proposed moratorium would have applied to final Common Council approval of new hyperscale or large-scale data center developments requiring discretionary council action or approval.
facts.supporting_summary: The text limits the proposed restriction to specified final council approvals, within the council's lawful authority.

facts.value: Reasonably anticipated components of a substantially related development would have been considered together when under common ownership or control, on the same or contiguous properties, sharing substantial infrastructure, or part of the same planned development.
facts.supporting_summary: The proposal addresses related phases, expansions, buildings, facilities, and other components when determining whether a development is covered.

facts.value: Facilities primarily providing telecommunications services or emergency communications infrastructure would not be classified as data centers. Lawfully granted prior approvals would remain undisturbed, and study, discussion, planning, and review could continue without covered final council approval.
facts.supporting_summary: The text excludes specified communications facilities, preserves prior approvals, and permits non-final activities.

facts.value: The moratorium would have begun upon passage and lasted no more than 365 days, subject to earlier termination.
facts.supporting_summary: The duration and effective-date provisions are proposed terms; the minutes report that the measure failed.

facts.value: The proposed moratorium would have ended at the earliest of effective zoning amendments establishing relevant definitions and standards, subsequent council repeal or termination, or 365 days after passage. Extension beyond 365 days would require subsequent council action.
facts.supporting_summary: Section 4 specifies three termination events and requires a separate council action for an extension.

facts.value: The proposal requested Planning Services to recommend zoning-code amendments during the proposed moratorium, in consultation with relevant departments, utilities, officials, experts, and CIERC upon its establishment.
facts.supporting_summary: Suggested review topics included definitions, zoning and approvals, site standards, backup power, resource demands, infrastructure capacity, environmental impacts, and full buildout.

facts.value: Other governmental bodies with approval authority would have been requested, within applicable law, to consider corresponding temporary measures; the proposal did not direct action beyond their legal authority.
facts.supporting_summary: The proposal framed corresponding measures by other bodies as a request subject to legal authority.

facts.value: The separate CIERC creation resolution, G-26-09-16 As Amended As Amended, failed 3–5. Ayes: Booker, Jehl, Paddock. Nays: Bender, Chambers, Ensley, Hartman, Myers. Mayor signature: N/A.
facts.supporting_summary: Entry III concerns the proposed Community Infrastructure & Environmental Review Commission, not the data center moratorium vote in entry IV.

facts.value: The proposal has unsigned lines for Council Member Rohli Booker and Council Attorney Joseph G. Bonahoom.
facts.supporting_summary: The final page names Booker and Bonahoom beneath blank signature lines.
